articles.title: OpenAI training its next-gen AI models on real-world tasks by contractors: Report
articles.lede: OpenAI training its next-gen AI models on real-world tasks by contractors: Report. OpenAI is looking to improve the real-world usefulness of its next-generation AI models by training them on data drawn from everyday tasks. The ChatGPT maker has partnered with training data company Handshake AI to collect data from third-party contractors based on the real work they did in their previous and current job roles, according to a report by Wired. The data collection is part of OpenAI’s efforts to compare the performance of its AI models against an established human baseline for various tasks. CCIA voices concerns over proposed Washington state regulation on high-risk artificial intelligence
articles.lede:
CCIA voices concerns over proposed Washington state regulation on high-risk artificial intelligence.

The Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA) testified before the Washington House Technology, Economic Development, & Veterans Committee to oppose House Bill 2157. The bill proposes comprehensive regulations for so-called “high-risk” artificial intelligence systems. CCIA argued that while the intention behind responsible AI governance is positive, the bill’s ambiguous definitions and extensive requirements could lead to legal uncertainty, higher costs, and slower innovation across Washington.

articles.title: Huawei matches Nvidia in China's AI chip market, 2026 power shift in play
articles.lede: Soaring demand for high-end computing power, combined with geopolitical pressure and supply-chain constraints, is reshaping China's AI chip market at a structural level. Bernstein estimates that Huawei's share of China's AI chip market rose from about one-third of Nvidia's level in 2024 to reach parity with Nvidia in 2025. The shift marks a new phase in which domestic suppliers are taking the lead.
